ashley: hey team — since the 03:40 deploy some auth calls are intermittently returning 502 / 502 gateway and spikes to 3s+ latency. example request id I pulled from the client: req_0a9f3c. happens on /v1/auth/token and sometimes /v1/generate. billing/keys look fine. can we get a quick repro checklist?
sam: thanks — can you paste the raw request-id(s) and a quick curl you used? also confirm the region (us-west1/us-east1) and whether this is hosted or Dedicated.
ashley: hosted, us-west1. here's the minimal curl I ran (sanitized):

```bash
API_KEY=REDACTED
curl -i -X POST https://inference.redwood.ai/v1/auth/token \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $API_KEY" \
  -H "X-Request-ID: req_0a9f3c" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"grant_type":"client_credentials"}'
```

response headers I got: 
```
HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway
Content-Type: application/json
X-Request-ID: req_0a9f3c
X-Trace-Id: trace-9a7b
Retry-After: 0

{"error":"upstream_error","message":"bad gateway"}
```

jun: copying — can you also run the same with `-v` and paste the raw header handshake? helps us see if it's TLS/backend timing.
sam: while you do that, please also run these quick SDK minimal repros (one-liners) so we can rule out client library bugs. replace API_KEY and REQUEST_ID placeholders.

PYTHON (requests):
```python
import requests
url = "https://inference.redwood.ai/v1/auth/token"
headers = {"Authorization": "Bearer API_KEY", "X-Request-ID": "REQUEST_ID", "Content-Type": "application/json"}
payload = {"grant_type": "client_credentials"}
r = requests.post(url, json=payload, headers=headers, timeout=10)
print(r.status_code, r.headers.get('X-Request-ID'))
print(r.text)
```

NODE (fetch):
```js
const fetch = require('node-fetch');
(async () => {
  const res = await fetch('https://inference.redwood.ai/v1/auth/token', {
    method: 'POST',
    headers: { 'Authorization': 'Bearer API_KEY', 'X-Request-ID': 'REQUEST_ID', 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
    body: JSON.stringify({ grant_type: 'client_credentials' }),
    timeout: 10000
  });
  console.log(res.status, res.headers.get('x-request-id'));
  console.log(await res.text());
})();
```

GO (net/http):
```go
package main
import (
  "bytes"
  "fmt"
  "io/ioutil"
  "net/http"
  "time"
)
func main() {
  client := &http.Client{Timeout: 10 * time.Second}
  req, _ := http.NewRequest("POST", "https://inference.redwood.ai/v1/auth/token", bytes.NewBufferString(`{"grant_type":"client_credentials"}`))
  req.Header.Set("Authorization", "Bearer API_KEY")
  req.Header.Set("X-Request-ID", "REQUEST_ID")
  req.Header.Set("Content-Type", "application/json")
  resp, err := client.Do(req)
  if err != nil { panic(err) }
  defer resp.Body.Close()
  b, _ := ioutil.ReadAll(resp.Body)
  fmt.Println(resp.StatusCode, resp.Header.Get("X-Request-ID"))
  fmt.Println(string(b))
}
```

sam: if those reproduce, pls attach the stdout and the full response headers. also collect a debug bundle from the host side — steps below (hosted customers: collect and paste any `X-Trace-Id` and request timestamp):

- grab server trace id from response header (e.g., X-Trace-Id: trace-9a7b).
- attach the client side curl `-v` output.
- run these on your machine and paste output (sanitized):
```bash
# grep for request id in logs
ssh jump-host "grep -R \"req_0a9f3c\" /var/log/redwood || true" > client_req.log
# collect recent system logs (last 1k lines)
journalctl -u redwood -n 1000 --no-pager > redwood_journal.log
```

sre-bot: incident-note: collected metric spike at 2026-03-16T03:40:10Z (latency 3.2s) — flagged for infra-team.

ashley: ran python snippet — got 502, X-Trace-Id: trace-9a7b. pasted curl -v to the thread (see attached gist). also found token service returning 502 intermittently across 03:39-03:46 window. attaching client logs now.
sam: perfect — one more ask: can you run the go snippet with `REQUEST_ID=req_0a9f3c` and `API_KEY` set and drop output here, then I'll escalate to runtime and include the trace id and the debug bundle links. if you can't paste full logs, at least paste the request/response headers and the small stack trace if present. :thumbsup:

ashley: will do, thanks. pinging when done.
